customManagers.description: The OpenJDK 25 source (own upstream), moved as GA alone: a jdk25u GA tag, jdk-25.X.Y[.Z[.W]]-ga, which also names CA respins such as jdk-25.0.5.0.3-ga, and never an EA build (ruling R46). .github/workflows/pins-bot.yml then fills REF and DIGEST (scripts/resolve-ga.sh: the build tag and commit GA names) and TARBALL_SHA256 on the PR's branch; until it has, build/derive-upstream-version.sh refuses to give a version and every build stops. UPSTREAM_VERSION is derived from REF, not managed here.
clang22, the compiler every build uses; a bump rebuilds and releases.
ca-certs, the family's CA roots: lib/security/cacerts is built from its release's trusted roots, so a bump ships new roots and releases.
longboat, CI only: installed-arm64 installs it because clang22-cross's preinstall requires it. Nothing of it ships, so a bump re-runs CI and releases nothing.

The boot JDK (Temurin 25 GA, macOS aarch64 tar.gz): a build input whose files do not ship, but it compiles the shipped classes and writes their jars' Created-By, so it is declared state and a bump makes reconcile cut a repackage. TAG and the asset's SHA-256 move together (github-release-attachments); build/toolchain.sh derives the download URL from TAG.

pandoc (macOS arm64 zip), which configure uses to make the man pages: a build input whose files do not ship, but the man pages it makes do, so it is declared state and a bump makes reconcile cut a repackage. VERSION and the asset's SHA-256 move together (github-release-attachments); build/toolchain.sh's jdk_pandoc derives the download URL from VERSION.

jtreg, the OpenJDK test harness tests/jtreg.sh runs the conformance subset with: a test tool only, nothing of it ships. jtreg publishes no binaries, so build/toolchain.sh's jdk_jtreg builds GitHub's tarball of TAG, verified by SHA256. Renovate moves TAG but cannot hash the tarball: the PR must write SHA256 (shasum -a 256 of https://github.com/openjdk/jtreg/archive/refs/tags/<TAG>.tar.gz) before it merges; until then the fetch refuses the stale pin.

The previous jdk-25 release, which tests/smoke-mavericks.sh installs before the candidate for its upgrade leg: a test input only, nothing of it ships. It reads 'none' until the first release exists; the regex matches only a version, so Renovate proposes nothing until a maintainer writes the first release's tag here, and then moves it to each newer release. A tag such as 25.0.5.0.3-mavericks.4 has six numbers and Renovate's regex versioning compares five, so the versioning leaves out the 25 every jdk-25 tag starts with and compares the -mavericks.N as revision.

GNU autoconf, which the jdk source's configure runs to generate itself: a build input whose files do not ship, but the configure it generates shapes the build, so it is declared state and a bump makes reconcile cut a repackage. build/toolchain.sh's jdk_autoconf fetches the release tarball of VERSION from ftp.gnu.org, verified by SHA256, and builds it on the pinned GNU m4. Renovate reads releases from Savannah's git tags (vX.Y, never the vX.Yz betas) but cannot hash the tarball: the PR must write SHA256 before it merges; until then the fetch refuses the stale pin.

GNU m4, which the pinned autoconf runs (it needs 1.4.8 or later; /usr/bin/m4 is 1.4.6 on Mac OS X 10.9 and on modern macOS): a build input whose files do not ship, but it shapes the generated configure, so it is declared state and a bump makes reconcile cut a repackage. build/toolchain.sh's jdk_autoconf fetches the release tarball of VERSION from ftp.gnu.org, verified by SHA256, and builds it. Renovate reads releases from Savannah's git tags (vX.Y.Z, never the betas) but cannot hash the tarball: the PR must write SHA256 before it merges.

packageRules.description: Only jdk25u GA tags of the 25 update train (jdk-25.X.Y[.Z[.W]]-ga, five parts for a CA respin such as 25.0.5.0.3) are proposed; build tags (jdk-25.X.Y+N, which include every EA build) and the next release's tags are not (ruling R46). REF, DIGEST and the tarball pin are filled by .github/workflows/pins-bot.yml on the PR's branch.
prBodyNotes: **The source pins:** `.github/workflows/pins-bot.yml` writes `REF`, `DIGEST` (`scripts/resolve-ga.sh`) and `TARBALL_SHA256` in `components/jdk/version` on this branch. Until it has, every build stops at `build/derive-upstream-version.sh`. If the bot failed, run `sh scripts/resolve-ga.sh && sh scripts/pin-source-tarballs.sh` on this branch and push the file (INGREDIENTS.md).

**The jtreg pin:** a jdk25u bump whose `make/conf/github-actions.conf` names another `JTREG_VERSION` fails `release.yml`'s `source` job (`scripts/check-jtreg-pin.sh`) until `components/jtreg/version` moves with it: `TAG=jtreg-<that version>` and the `SHA256` of `https://github.com/openjdk/jtreg/archive/refs/tags/<TAG>.tar.gz`, on this branch.

packageRules.description: The boot JDK stays on Temurin 25 GA tags (jdk-25.X.Y[.Z]+N); the 26 train and early-access builds are never proposed. A bump changes the shipped class bytes and Created-By, so reconcile cuts a repackage.

jtreg is pinned to the version the pinned jdk25u's own CI runs (JTREG_VERSION in its make/conf/github-actions.conf), since a newer jtreg changes what its tests see (StackWalkTest counts jtreg's own frames); and its tarball SHA-256 is written by hand on the PR. So a jtreg bump never automerges.
prBodyNotes: **Merge only to match jdk25u:** take this bump only when the pinned jdk25u's `make/conf/github-actions.conf` names this `JTREG_VERSION`; otherwise close it. **The tarball pin:** write `SHA256` in `components/jtreg/version` on this branch: `curl -sSfL https://github.com/openjdk/jtreg/archive/refs/tags/<TAG>.tar.gz | shasum -a 256`, then `sh scripts/pin-jtreg-deps.sh` to pin this jtreg's build dependencies in `components/jtreg/deps`, then run `sh tests/jtreg.sh` on Mac OS X 10.9 against the current image (INGREDIENTS.md).

packageRules.description: GNU autoconf and m4 tarball SHA-256s are written by hand on the PR, so their bumps never automerge.
prBodyNotes: **The tarball pin:** write `SHA256` in this `components/<autoconf|m4>/version` on this branch: `curl -sSfL https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/<name>/<name>-<VERSION>.tar.gz | shasum -a 256`, checking it against GNU's `.sig` beside it. Then `sh tests/autoconf-test.sh` and a build (INGREDIENTS.md).
